_added: 2026-09-01, slice R05 of the Repo Hygiene Program (WR-000040).

handoff.reason: Hosted-CI workflow files are the master plan's CI/CD hardening owner's surface; R05's authority is explicitly build-only with no hosted-CI or Actions changes. The finding is real: the edge-liveness job installs psycopg unpinned while every other workflow installs requirements.lock, so this one job can resolve a different psycopg than the suite it is checking. Carried to that owner in out/repo-hygiene-program/r05-contract-change-draft.md.

exempt.reason: DELIBERATE, and the reasoning is written down in ops/ci-dep-check.py's header: requirements.txt is the human-facing declaration whose environment markers keep Dell's older runtime installing correctly, requirements.lock is the pinned output CI installs. 'CI installs the lock; a human installs the txt.' migrate-dell.sh bootstraps a HUMAN'S machine, so forcing one machine's resolution onto it is the thing that header refuses. Revisit only together with that decision.

Toolchain bootstrap on the last-resort path, not a project dependency: it is reached only when the machine has NO Python new enough to build the venv at all, and it installs uv purely to fetch a standalone CPython. There is no lockfile that could pin it, because it runs before this repo's runtime exists. Named in out/repo-hygiene-program/r05-contract-change-draft.md as a candidate for a pinned version by migrate-dell.sh's owner; R05's write set does not include the Dell migration path.

Opt-in developer rig, installed into its own throwaway .venv-tts and shared with nothing: it is not on any worktree, CI or deploy path. No lockfile exists for it, and generating one needs a network resolution R05 could not perform (the session's egress guard refused the package index host). Recorded as an open item in out/repo-hygiene-program/r05-contract-change-draft.md rather than left invisible.
